status: Protocol only. No benchmark run, evaluator weight, download, provider call or paid generation is authorized by this file. Every head-to-head outcome is NOT TESTED until a valid matched run exists.

statistics.preferenceInterval: prompt-cluster bootstrap: raters and seeds nested within prompt; percentile intervals with linear interpolation. Rater effects crossed across prompts are not modelled (a limitation of version 1).
statistics.winRule: Holm-adjusted p-value < alpha in the product's favour, and the declared success floor (required for preference cohorts, may be 0) met by the product's success rate lower bound over prompt clusters; the interval at the cohort's Holm step level is reported for reference
statistics.loseRule: Holm-adjusted p-value < alpha in the comparator's favour
statistics.matchRule: no significant difference, and a margin declared before analysis on the endpoint's own scale, with the two one-sided interval at alpha / m (m = the Holm family) inside it
statistics.otherwise: INCONCLUSIVE; a failure to detect a difference is never MATCHES
statistics.ties: a tie counts as half a vote for each side
statistics.refusals: kept in the denominator of completion rates with their cause code; never dropped
statistics.pilot: a 60-task creative pilot and a 5-8 person formative UX study estimate variance only; they establish no superiority
statistics.holmFamily: every cohort with records, declared before any label; a cohort blocked by its records counts with p = 1
statistics.intentionToTreat: each prompt-and-seed slot's outcome per product comes from its deciding trial under the cohort's declared analysis (firstAttempt: attempt 1; bestWithinBudget: the first successful attempt within the budget, retries following failures only); every slot weighs one (the mean of its raters' votes); in preference cohorts a slot one side failed counts as that side's loss and a slot both failed as a tie

sampling.note: Repeated raters and seeds are not independent prompts. Every slot where both products produced an output is shown to exactly ratersPerPair raters, as a pair naming each side's deciding trial. Increase the sample or report INCONCLUSIVE when power is inadequate; never shrink the corpus after seeing outcomes.

retries.policy: Every attempt is recorded with a contiguous attempt number (1..n, each once); a cohort declares firstAttempt or bestWithinBudget analysis, and the two are separate cohorts; every failure stays in the intention-to-treat denominator.

keep: original media (private evidence store for likeness/reference media)
retention.consent: Likeness and reference media need a consent from the observations' registry (unique consentId, the categories it covers, grantedAt <= deleteBy) that covers the cohort's category and has not passed its deleteBy date at analysis.

categories.name: Professional editing
categories.tasks: S/M/L/H/A/K profiles; deterministic edit scripts and human finishing briefs
categories.measures: canonical expected edits, frame/sample boundaries, export decode, task time and errors, professional editor rubric
categories.gate: no data loss or silent effect loss; fixed policy passes on the claimed profile; comparative time/preference interval

categories.name: Text-to-video
categories.tasks: 240 balanced prompts after the pilot; common duration and resolution; audio and silent separately
categories.measures: prompt fulfilment, motion/physics/artifact proxies, blind preference, usable-take rate
categories.gate: adjusted 95% lower preference bound > 0.5 with the safety/task success floor

categories.name: Image-to-video
categories.tasks: matched licensed reference images, poses, first/last constraints
categories.measures: reference preservation, motion/control adherence, temporal artifacts, blind comparison
categories.gate: as B; unsupported controls scored separately

categories.name: Generative editing
categories.measures: source preservation outside the edit, semantic success, temporal/audio continuity, human review
categories.gate: no unrelated edit accepted silently; matched task-quality interval

categories.name: Cinematic control
categories.tasks: camera/lens/light intents, fixed reference scenes and trajectories where supported
categories.measures: framing/trajectory error, labelled optical proxies, blinded cinematographer judgment
categories.gate: intent-to-control agreement plus measured adherence; metadata-only fails an applied-control claim

categories.name: Character and scene continuity
categories.tasks: repeated consented subjects/environments over 3-8 shots, held-out poses and light
categories.measures: identity/scene embedding proxies, human same-identity and continuity ratings
categories.gate: pack/version correctness mandatory; a pixel identity claim needs a human interval and failure rate

categories.name: A/V synchronization
categories.tasks: speech/percussion/action clips with known onsets; silent and native audio distinct
categories.measures: frame/sample onset offsets, lip/audio alignment proxies, listening/viewing rubric
categories.gate: profile drift bound; native-language review for dubbing; no universal sync claim

categories.name: Agentic production
categories.tasks: 20 pilot briefs, then powered matched projects; imported assets first, generated later
categories.measures: editable project completion, tool failures, retries, intervention minutes, restart/revision success
categories.gate: every accepted action authorized; no fake completion or double billing; 95% task-success interval

categories.name: Privacy and recovery
categories.tasks: fault injection: crash, kill, ENOSPC, reparse, ACL, backup/restore, offline egress capture
categories.measures: exact acknowledged state and assets, denied unauthorized access, no orphans, restore completeness
categories.gate: all required negative controls pass on the supported Windows artifact; no average hides a safety failure

categories.name: UX and task completion
categories.tasks: six journeys, Arabic/English, novice and editor cohorts
categories.measures: completion, errors, time, accessibility, workload/satisfaction, observations
categories.gate: no critical data-loss or accessibility issue; powered counterbalanced comparison before superiority

categories.name: Cost per finished video
categories.tasks: the same accepted deliverable including rejected takes, audio, upscale, export, storage
categories.measures: currency micro-units, credits with conversion, operator time, compute cost; actual receipts
categories.gate: no unapproved spend; cost per accepted minute with uncertainty; zero disabled inference is not a win

categories.name: Hardware and resource efficiency
categories.tasks: the same media, model, precision, settings and host; cold and warm cohorts
categories.measures: process-tree peak RAM/VRAM, disk/cache, energy if metered, wall time per finished minute
categories.gate: approved resource policy and cleanup pass; no inferred cross-hardware speedup

records.note: Version 1 analyses the primary endpoint only; costMicros and interventionSeconds are recorded for categories H and K and reported by later analyses.
